account:
It is day 1, about 09:16, and I am in the town hall after a quiet morning office session. I have read both appointment books and returned them to their chest. My next appointment is the mill grain inspection at 10:00, followed by lunch at home, council letters at 13:00, tea with the neighbour at the east-bank cottage at 15:00, and office at 16:30. The innkeeper will meet me in my office at 17:45 before the 18:00 great hall lighting inspection with the builder.

There are hints of preparations I have not been fully told about. The secretary reported that the innkeeper collected bread from the baker and said the inn owes forty-four emeralds, payable after the jubilee. The secretary did not establish who ordered it or its exact purpose. Freight asked that their arrangements stay private until today at eighteen. That timing matches the lighting inspection, and the bread and mention of a jubilee make me suspect preparations for a gathering or celebration, possibly involving the hall. This is only a suspicion; I have not seen the arrangements or confirmed that these matters are connected. The innkeeper has been attentive to confirming our evening meeting, while the neighbour confirmed our usual tea and said no special preparations were needed.

The secretary and I have found no separate correspondence or office records. The treasury contained only 128 emeralds, which I left untouched. No one has requested an audience and the secretary reports no new public business. I recently heard the baker shouting in the distance but could not understand the words, so I cannot infer what it concerned. For now I should keep my appointments, starting with the mill, and learn more through what people actually tell or show me rather than treating my suspicions as fact.
